issues: Everything is up on last week: sales crossed £40,000 again and are tracking the same this week, with delivery and covers both up.
Spend per head is strong; staff are pushing edamame as a sharer while guests look at menus to add about another £5 to each bill.
Wages were 21.9%, close to target, after extra staff were added for the school holidays at a cost of £2,434, which the site has been told it can spend.

The drinks variance has been fixed: matcha was newly added to Kobas and showed about three bags down because a full year of variance since opening was added at once; Dave corrected it and some invoice issues were also fixed.
Loyalty member bills are up, although many of the same people are coming in with new accounts.
Reviews were all five stars with no negatives.
Delivery: no reviews, but two missing items; one was disputed successfully and the other was not approved.
Deliveroo had one red line for Sunday prep time at 22 minutes, both missing items happened at weekends, and a low rating complained of cold food and dry noodles.

The GM checked the timestamps: the first order was collected within a minute of being marked ready, but riders pick up several bags and drive 15 to 20 minutes to the city centre on multi drop runs, which may explain the cold food.
Amy asked the site to assign someone to focus on the pass and delivery at the same time when busy, as with low delivery volume a single complaint drags down the whole rating.

Hiring: a new starter joins this weekend; the GM and Inka are waiting on a second FOH supervisor trial shift to decide who is more suitable; two more candidates were seen today and one will join next week.
Cockroaches were found in three restaurants in the Oasis food court; EHO visited all sites on 26/10 and found no trace at Maki Meadowhall, so the site stays open.

Meadowhall centre is arranging Rentokil to put sticky strips on the floors of all restaurants as a precaution; if pests are found in the centre itself the whole Oasis closes for three weeks, and so far one of the three restaurants has reopened after fumigation while two stay closed for another week.

Sophie reported the Deliveroo reset at Maki 14 was done over the weekend; improvement is tracked daily on the dashboard and the reset sites have shown continuous green lights for two weeks (Admin Meeting 26/10).

Delivery extra items at Meadowhall print only at the ramen section printer, so FOH have to carry tickets to the back kitchen; Inka will call Sophie about changing the Kobas printer settings (Admin Meeting 26/10).
Michael said Meadowhall is targeted at £3 million a year but is tracking at about £2 million and has not grown for a year, and asked for a plan for the site (Admin Meeting 26/10).

Inka said Deliveroo ratings swing heavily because volume is only five or six orders a week, so a single refund case can drop the rating to 2.5; Michael noted a 2.5 rating and 19.5 minute prep time the previous week, now back at 4 (Admin Meeting 26/10).

Growth plans: the team is targeting Sheffield city centre student accommodation for the first time after B2B approaches to businesses around Meadowhall got no replies, wants the 2 km Deliveroo radius extended to student areas, and Inka has emailed Meadowhall centre marketing for promotional support because the mall allows no signage, pop ups or street activity (Admin Meeting 26/10).
Persistent food quality issues at Meadowhall were reviewed by Michael and Sophie, and Sophie will look at the site during her visit (Sophie x Mike meeting 23/10).

Region: the new Christmas set menu (including a set menu for large bookings) brings three new dishes; head chefs must check stock and have everything ready by Friday 30/10, leaflets must be ready by Friday (nudge marketing if they are late) and an allergy sheet is needed for the new dishes.
Region: the lunch deal continues through half term this week on a flexible basis, offered only when customers ask for it.
Region: the £5 ramen promotion ends on Saturday 31/10, and a new loyalty tier promotion will follow, probably announced at next Tuesday's KPI meeting.
Region: delivery prep times have improved overall across the region; this week's focus is disputing inaccurate orders as quickly as possible.
Amy said Meadowhall missed its weekly sales target, although half term made it very busy (AM Updates 28/10).
Wage and food costs were both green, quoted at 21% (AM Updates 28/10).
Delivery ratings suffered from cold food and packaging complaints on busy weekends, so staff were told to prioritise delivery tasks on the waiter section at peak times (AM Updates 28/10).
Inka said suggesting edamame to 70% to 80% of seated tables has been highly successful at Meadowhall and will be spread to the other regions (AM Updates 28/10).
B2B catering pushes are planned for mid November (AM Updates 28/10).

Region: Amy said sales improved with the student promotions and half term, food costs stayed high from the volume of frozen ramen bought, and delivery ratings fell on cold food complaints and long rider waits (AM Updates 28/10).
Region: Michael clarified that the £5 ramen offer does not simply end this week, as customers still have 14 days from their sign up date to redeem it (AM Updates 28/10).
